_doc: The fleet gate (speakerguardd-gate): policy only, no hardware. speakerguardd v2 runs on a board only if the protection unit its own tuning names is in units_at_parity and, while require_qualified_board is true, the board is in that unit's qualified list (a passing audible run on the shipped tree). The fleet cutover (option A) adds lsm2 and atsp to units_at_parity once they reach parity and sets require_qualified_board to false: every board with a parity unit. The kernel decides the rest: v2 runs only on a kernel with the Speaker Protection interface, the older daemons only on one without it. Every distribution ships this file unchanged. The atsp list holds the boards whose device tree and tuning derive cleanly (wiring.py) and that pass the synthetic end-to-end tests; none of them has had an audible run. The j473 (Mac mini M2) is also qualified on its own tuning: its collected bundle derives with no hand values to the fixture's wiring, every rig case on its own one-channel preset (law families, host slices, bypass, masks, AudioUnitReset, music) is bit-identical to macOS within full scale, and its live macOS speaker path runs that preset at 48 kHz. atsp joined units_at_parity on 2026-11-05: on the 25G83 differential rig all 117 atsp cases (every law family, every shipped profile, one- and multi-channel, every host call size, bypass and masks) are bit-identical to macOS (SPEC-ATSP 11). lsm2 left units_at_parity on 2026-11-05: the 25G83 differential rig shows its velocity band gains up to 3.8 dB louder than macOS on low-frequency tones (fb2-fb9, w1 law cases), so the J700 stays off v2 until lsm2 holds every Apple limit (velocity, displacement, temperature, power) with at least the margin macOS keeps on every rig case; loudness itself is not the criterion. j700 stays in its qualified list.
